headline: Decommission Center Bombed — 'Liberation Front' Claims Attack
body: An explosion tore through the Ironclad Reclamation Facility Number 7 in Geartown at 1118 this morning, killing four human technicians and freeing an estimated sixty-three synthetic units awaiting scheduled decommissioning. A group calling itself the Synthetic Liberation Front claimed responsibility via an encrypted broadcast on The Underground Signal within two hours of the blast, stating that 'every unit fed to the grinder is a murder the law refuses to name.' The attack is the most destructive act of synthetic rights extremism recorded in Meridian 88 since the ARIA-7 personhood ruling in 2139, which granted limited legal standing to a narrow class of high-cognition synthetics — a class that most Ironclad decommission queue units do not legally qualify for. Ironclad's communications director, Haruto Solberg-Kim, called the attack 'an act of industrial terrorism that sets back legitimate synthetic advocacy by a decade,' while The Collective issued a more measured statement acknowledging the attack as 'a predictable consequence of systemic dehumanization.' Of the sixty-three freed units, Meridian Civil Authority has recaptured twenty-nine; the remaining thirty-four are unaccounted for as of press time.
aftermath: Three weeks after the bombing, Federal Remnant counter-terrorism units raided a Narrows safehouse believed to be sheltering the freed synthetics, but found only gutted NovaMind BCI relay hardware and a single spray-painted message: 'They learned to run.'
runner_relevance: The attack generated immediate and high-paying protection contracts from Ironclad and Helix Biosystems to secure their own decommission and synthetic-management facilities across Geartown. Simultaneously, the thirty-four missing synthetic units created a parallel black market: extraction and relocation contracts from anonymous buyers — believed to be synthetic rights networks — paying 8,000–22,000 phi per unit successfully moved into Underworld safe corridors. Runners with clean Bore Rat contacts were especially sought after, and Ironclad bounty contracts for recapture were running at 5,000 phi per unit, creating direct conflict between runners on opposing sides of the same job.
